title: Session-replay wrappers; unify reauth telemetry and backoff templates across SDKs
author: Priya Sharma
description: Motivation: customer telemetry and internal ops showed multiple small breakages around auth refresh windows during long-lived streaming sessions. SDK teams requested a minimal, consistent surface for session-level replay and reauth so apps can replay or resume an idempotent stream after mid-session credential rotation without ad-hoc application code. This PR introduces a lightweight session-replay wrapper and consolidates reauth telemetry hooks and backoff templates across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Goals: 1) Provide a thin, well-documented wrapper that records replay checkpoints and exposes a deterministic resume API; 2) Unify reauth telemetry events so the control plane + observability tooling can correlate reauth cycles with stream restarts; 3) Offer opinionated backoff templates (fast/medium/conservative) consumers can opt into; 4) Bump SDK versions to snapshot releases for immediate downstream consumption. Summary of changes: - Added session_replay wrapper implementations and typed stream guard helpers to Python/TS/Go with the same public names and ergonomics; - Centralized reauth telemetry events (reauth_attempt, reauth_success, reauth_failure, replay_resume) and standardized attributes across SDKs; - Introduced three backoff presets (fast, balanced, conservative) that feed into retry profiles for streaming operations; - Updated SDK examples and e2e test harness to include deterministic replay tests and a simulated credential rotation harness; - Version bumps: py 2.3.0-rc1, ts 1.8.2-rc1, go v1.5.0-rc1; - Added migration guide and upgrade tests. Checklist: [x] API review with SDK leads [x] Observability schema registered [x] E2E replay test added [x] Backwards-compatible (no public API breaking) [x] Release notes drafted Rollout plan: merge to main -> publish rc packages behind feature flags -> smoke test for 48 hours -> promote to stable if no regression telemetry. Backports: none (no customer-facing bugfix required in older branches).
commit_summary: (1) introduce session replay wrapper and tests; (2) unify telemetry event schema; (3) add backoff templates and retry integration; (4) example updates; (5) version bumps and changelogs

Priya Sharma: Reply: telemetry schema added to internal/telemetry/telemetry_events.yaml and coordinated with observability. Attributes are stable and versioned.

release_notes: SDKs: Add session-replay wrapper and unified reauth telemetry. Introduce three streaming backoff templates (fast/balanced/conservative). Minor version bumps (py 2.3.0-rc1, ts 1.8.2-rc1, go v1.5.0-rc1). Backwards compatible. See docs/sdk/session-replay.md for migration details.
testing_performed: Unit tests added for replay checkpoints and eviction behavior across py/ts/go. Integration harness simulates credential rotation at various TTL offsets and asserts deterministic resume within the checkpoint window. Manual verified telemetry events in staging via observability dashboards. Load test: 2k concurrent streams with random rotations; <1.5% additional tail latency observed and no leakage after replay evictions.
upgrade_instructions: Clients: import session_replay wrapper and wrap existing streaming iterator/async generator. Default behavior is opt-in. To enable: Python: from redwood import session_replay; client.stream(..., session_wrapper=session_replay.wrap) TypeScript: import {wrapSession} from '@redwood/sdk'; client.stream({ sessionWrapper: wrapSession }) Go: session := replay.NewSession(client.Stream); See docs/sdk/session-replay.md for examples and opt-in toggles.
